plan: With a private value of $30, I want to win the auction but avoid overpaying. Since values are drawn randomly between $0-$20, most bidders will have lower values. My optimal strategy is to bid strategically - high enough to likely win, but not so high that I lose money. I'll bid close to, but slightly above, the expected maximum of other bidders' potential values. A bid around $19-$20 seems reasonable to maximize my chances of winning profitably.

My private value is $25, which is higher than the typical $0-$20 range. This suggests I should bid aggressively. However, rational bidders will also try to maximize profit. The optimal strategy is to bid just below my true value, anticipating others will bid strategically. Since the second-highest bid determines the payment, I'll bid close to but slightly under $25 to ensure winning while minimizing my payment.

My actual value is $22, but the game's value range is $0-$20. Since other bidders' values are randomly drawn from $0-$20, I want to bid strategically. A pure optimal strategy would be to bid just above the expected maximum opponent bid. With uniform distribution, the expected max opponent value is around $20. I'll bid slightly above that to ensure winning while minimizing overpayment.
